name: Hip Abduction
definition: A strict unilateral open-chain hip isolation performed side-lying on a treatment table, with a cuff weight just above the ankle, the lower support leg flexed, the working hip held in neutral sagittal and axial posture, and the straight working leg moving to 35 degrees of frontal-plane abduction while the toes remain forward. The directly reviewed fixture uses a pressure-biofeedback unit beneath the trunk to hold 35 to 45 mmHg and a horizontal contact band to mark the endpoint; both are part of the initial contract because every analyzed repetition used them. McBeth identifies the feedback as a substitution-control technique and cites prior work for its effect on gluteus-medius recruitment; McBeth did not itself compare feedback with no feedback. Gluteus medius is the sole primary and tensor fasciae latae is secondary. The exact gluteus-minimus region has no body-model surface and remains unassigned because anatomical capability alone does not establish its categorical role in this fixture; the unsplit gluteus-maximus profile likewise conservatively omits superior-fiber abduction. Those structures receive no proxy assignment, so the current 3D highlight and volume credit deliberately understate the complete abductor system. Standing, band, cable, machine, bodyweight-only, seated, internally or externally rotated, clamshell, lateral-walk, closed-chain, and multi-joint variants remain outside this contract.

exercises.name: Pressure-Biofeedback Side-Lying Hip Abduction
movementSteps: Lie on one side on a treatment table with the working leg on top, both hips facing straight ahead, the lower leg bent for stability, and a cuff weight secured just above the working ankle.
Place a pressure-biofeedback unit beneath your torso, inflate it to 40 mmHg, and keep it between 35 and 45 mmHg while a horizontal band marks the 35-degree stopping point.
Keep the pelvis and spine still, the working knee straight, and the toes pointing forward.
Raise the straight top leg directly out to the side until it contacts the stopping band.
Lower the leg under control without rolling the pelvis or turning the toes upward.
